applied.change: The quote check is per table row, not per adjacent id. It collects the backticked ids on a line and every quoted string on that line outside a code span, and requires each quotation to be verbatim (whitespace-collapsed) in at least one record the row itself cites; a quoted string on a row that cites nothing is a failure in its own right. The floor is on that whole population - `checked == quoted` and `checked >= 81` - so narrowing the regex fails the check instead of shrinking what it looks at, where the old `assert checked >= 40` was a floor on the 61 id-adjacent pairs. The two gap rows that quoted a record without citing it (G1, G2) now carry the citation; G1's quotation was attributed to the closures record and is in fact the questionnaire's durable-execution future state, so the row cites the questionnaire. provenance.json keeps the id-adjacent rule, because its rows carry no ids in prose and every string in a JSON line is delimited by quotes. Falsified: re-planting the R75PROGRESS-001 wording at README.md:21 turns section 13 red (passed 126, failed 1), which the old check could not see.

The walk dispatches on the stage's declared `op`, never on its id. The five handlers are renamed for the operator they serve (`stage_sequence`, `stage_loop`, `stage_parallel`, `stage_approval`, `stage_effect`) and sit in a class-level `OPERATORS` table; `Run.check_operators()` runs before pricing and before any binding and refuses `document-invalid` 422, naming the stage, the op and both sets, for a stage whose operator nothing serves. The two other stage ids the runner re-typed are gone too: the effect stage is found by its `op` and the candidate step by the loop's declared judge step's `of`, so `run.py` now names no stage at all. E1's proof is the differential the row-75 boundary asks for: `out/p-canary.json` adds a sixth stage row that the loop's gate then depends on, and the run prices it into the plan's floor and worst case (5000 micros each), enters it second in declared order, commits `canary-step` and charges it - 12 committed steps against 11, spend 375000 against 370000 - with `"canary"` asserted absent from run.py. Falsified: restoring the id-keyed dispatch turns four checks red.

An expiry is terminal rather than a replayable step outcome. The gate step now commits `{outcome: expired, deadline_at: <the declared instant>}`, and `stage_approval()`'s replay path, on finding that outcome, re-parks the gate, re-reports `input-required`, sets the disposition through the gate and re-raises the same `deadline-exceeded` 504 with the deadline read off the step record. New checks run the human and the schedule envelopes a second time against their own state directories and assert the last line, the exit status, the disposition, the outcome, the stop reason, the run key and the problem type identical, with every step replayed and none executed. The lifecycle is asserted rather than assumed to be identical: the schedule door reports `input-required` again, and the human door - whose gate was decided, not expired - does not, because a decided gate is replayed and nobody is asked twice. Falsified: disabling the expired arm turns the redelivery check red (escalate then reject, as the review measured).

`on_cap` is read at the cap: it is the disposition the caller is answered with, set through the new `dispose()` gate, so the closed set it is checked against is the ontology's four. The problem type stays a function of which cap was hit, which is the errors capability's to say and not the document's, and the refusal sentence now names the disposition it produced rather than merely echoing the member. `out/p-iter1-reject.json` declares `reject` where the shipped unit declares `escalate`: the differential asserts the same `loop-terminated` record, the same 504 type and status, and two different dispositions. The member has a row in section 3's field table and an extension point (E9). Falsified: hardcoding `escalate` turns the on_cap check red.

`run()` writes its exit status to `out/<name>.rc` beside the report, and a new check walks every rc/report pair: 0 is completed with spend and no problem body, 2 is a problem body with zero spend, 3 is failed with spend, with all three codes required to occur over at least twenty pairs. The README row says the rule is measured as a mapping and names the section. Falsified: returning 2 unconditionally on a refusal turns that check red along with the door checks.

provenance.json says seven failure types, which is what the artifacts hold, and the numbers check now reads both files: ten counts written in words - four in README.md, six in provenance.json - each compared against the number read back out of the artifacts that describe it. A count that drifts in either file now fails in the file it drifted in.

The check asserts instead of printing, over the scope of its own sentence. It walks every file under `out/` including every executor and register state directory, requires the criterion and rubric member names (`must_contain`, `required_steps`, `required_tools`, `answer_contains`) to appear nowhere, parses each line that carries the criterion's phrase and requires every occurrence to sit under a candidate step's own `text` key, and prints how many files it scanned and how many carry the phrase. The dead `if False` line is gone. A second check at the end of section 13 makes the member-name half of the claim over the finished tree (200+ artifacts), because section 4 can only see what has run by then. Falsified: recording a rubric body onto the `judge-verdict` record turns three checks red.

`Run.dispose()` is the one place a disposition is set, refusing `document-invalid` for a word outside `DISPOSITIONS` the way `move()` does for task states; every literal assignment in `run.py` and in `main()` goes through it. A new check in section 1 parses the four words out of the `| Disposition |` row of docs/reference/ontology.md, asserts run.py's tuple equals them, asserts exactly one assignment site remains, and asserts every report's disposition is a member with at least three distinct ones reached. Falsified: restoring one bare `self.disposition = "retry"` turns it red.

The gate-expiry check computes the instant from the envelope's `occurred_at` plus the declared minutes and asserts the parked deadline equals it, so a hardcoded 1440 or a hardcoded instant fails. The differential the rule asks for is `out/p-deadline60.json`: the same schedule door against a unit declaring 60 minutes stamps a deadline 1380 minutes from the 1440-minute one, both read off the `approval-parked` records, and each refusal names its own. Falsified: stamping `timedelta(minutes=1440)` turns the differential red.

`harnesses.operators()` is called rather than dead: `run.py` reads `operator_names()` over examples/end-to-end/schemas/workflow.schema.json into `CAPABILITY_OPS` and declares `LOCAL_OPS = ("effect",)` beside it, and `check_operators()` refuses on every run if a handler key is in neither set, so the walk's dispatch table cannot drift from the schema. The check reads the capability's set from the schema itself, asserts the refusal detail names it, and asserts the shipped unit's one operator outside it is exactly `effect`. That `effect` is not one of the six the schema admits is written up as gap G12 with a research query rather than papered over; section 5 gains a row for where the vocabulary comes from. Falsified: adding a `branch` key to the handler table refuses every unit in the suite (passed 27, failed 100).

The sentence now says what holds - the judge step to read and the verdict to compare against are the document's, the vocabulary the judge answers in is the judge's - and the differential the rule asks for is `out/p-greenverdict.json`: a unit exiting on `green` runs all three permitted iterations, terminates `iteration_ceiling` with `last_verdict` `pass`, and names `green` in its refusal, while the shipped unit exits on the judge's verdict. That the verdict set is declared nowhere is gap G13 with a research query.

Both disabled statements are gone, and a third the review did not name (`assert sealed["outcomes"] if False else True` in section 7, which would have raised KeyError had it ever been enabled) with them. `grep -n 'if False' test.sh run.py` now returns nothing. The resume-correlation check gained the assertion the disabled line was reaching for and could not have: `out/crash-a.rep.json` does not exist, because the killed process never wrote a report - which is asserted, so a crash that returned instead of dying fails there too.

notes: The example's own count moved 111 -> 131 and FLOOR, provenance.visible_checks_counted and the README's run-step 1 promise moved with it; all three are asserted equal by section 13.

Behaviour a later reader would be surprised by: an envelope whose release gate expired now refuses the same way on every resubmission against its own state, so a checker that ran the schedule door twice and read `disposition=reject` (the walk carrying `expired` forward as a gate outcome) now reads `disposition=escalate` and a 504 both times. The lifecycle is not identical across a redelivery on the human door, and that is deliberate: a gate already decided is replayed and never parks again, so `input-required` appears once at the first run and not at the second, while an expired gate parks and expires again.

The refusal a bad operator raises is new and lands early: a unit declaring a stage `op` the composition capability's schema does not admit and this area does not add is refused `document-invalid` 422 with zero spend and no executor state directory, before pricing. An outside check that fed this runner a pipeline with an invented operator and expected a traceback (or a walked stage) now gets a problem body.

The cap refusal's detail sentence changed shape: it now reads "...; the unit declares on_cap 'escalate', so the disposition is escalate, and the proposed type ... is urn:agentic:problem:iteration-ceiling-reached". A grep for the old `; on_cap is escalate,` phrasing misses it.

Two members the review ranked as a habit rather than a finding - `outcome_on_success` and `reaches_outside`, both read but proved by no differential - now have differentials and field-table rows, and `summary`, which nothing reads, joins `carries` in the carried-and-not-consumed row and in gap G7; the carries differential deletes both members. This is beyond the fourteen findings and is recorded here so the ceremony's count of applied findings is not read as the count of changes.

Two gaps were added rather than mechanisms invented: G12 (`effect` is outside the composition capability's closed operator set, so this area declares it as a local addition beside it) and G13 (the verdict vocabulary a judge answers in is declared nowhere, so an unreachable loop exit runs to its cap instead of being refused). Both carry research queries.
